content.text: Digital creators often face significant hurdles when trying to set up online stores, especially in regions where platforms like Stripe are unavailable. The problem is clear: you need a robust solution that allows for seamless [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/get-crypto-payments-tanzanian-online-sellers-working-today-3|crypto]] payments and full ownership of your data. This guide details how to utilize Supabase as the order database for your digital store, allowing you to deploy infrastructure that works when conventional platforms fail. With COREMERCH's resources, you can set up your store without limitations, entirely removing reliance on traditional payment processors.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

In countries where conventional payment platforms are restricted, the need for resilient infrastructure is paramount. Supabase provides a powerful backend that handles order management seamlessly, ensuring you retain complete control over your data. By leveraging GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-14|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] Pages for hosting and integrating NOWPayments for crypto transactions, you create a self-sufficient digital store. This [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-github-pages-free-digital-product-15|The Real]] not only circumvents the limitations of platforms like Stripe but also guarantees ownership and sovereignty over your operations.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, gather the essential tools: a GitHub account for hosting your site, a Supabase account for order management, and a NOWPayments account for accepting crypto payments. Familiarize yourself with the Sovereign Blueprint to understand the deployment process. Ensure you have your digital products ready for upload. This preparation is vital to streamline your setup. Following these steps will position you for a successful deployment that meets the demands of your market.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Start by configuring your Supabase database to handle orders efficiently. Set up the necessary tables and schemas for your products and transactions. Next, integrate NOWPayments into your workflow to facilitate crypto transactions. It’s essential to test this payment layer rigorously to ensure all transactions are processed correctly. Utilize webhook notifications from NOWPayments to trigger order confirmations. Finally, set up a reliable file delivery method through Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to ensure your customers receive their products instantly after payment.
Own your infrastructure, don't rent it.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your infrastructure is configured, it’s time to go live. Promote your digital store through social media and other channels, directing potential customers to your hosted site. Monitor the payment process closely during your initial transactions. Confirm that orders are processed smoothly and customers receive their purchases without issues. This phase is crucial for building trust with your customers and ensuring a positive user experience. Document any challenges you face to refine your process for future transactions.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

With your digital store operational, consider scaling your offerings. You can add more products, enhance your marketing strategies, and explore additional channels for customer outreach. Supabase allows for easy database management, so increasing your product range is straightforward. Additionally, consider upgrading to the Edge Commerce Stack for advanced features, including SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration for better email deliverability. This will enhance your store’s professionalism and increase customer trust, allowing you to grow sustainably.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Deploy your digital store in hours, not weeks.

The setup decision comes down to time versus depth. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything to build Stack 01 yourself in an afternoon or Stack 02 over a weekend — full source code, step-by-step configuration, and the NOWPayments integration guide. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH build Stack 02 for you in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured for email deliverability. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. Both are at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.
